verses.text: From Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by God's will, sent to tell about the promise of life that is in Christ Jesus.
To Timothy, my dear son. Grace, mercy and peace to you from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
I thank God, whom I serve with a clear conscience, as my ancestors did. Night and day I keep remembering you in my prayers.
I remember your tears, and I long to see you, so that I may be filled with joy.
I remember your faith that is real. It lived first in your grandmother Lois and in your mother Eunice, and I am sure it lives in you too.
That is why I remind you to stir up God's gift, like a fire, the gift that is in you since I laid my hands on you.
For God did not give us a spirit that makes us afraid. He gave us a spirit of power, love and self-control.
So do not be ashamed to speak about our Lord, or ashamed of me, his prisoner. Instead, share with me in suffering for the Good News, by the power of God.
God saved us and called us to a holy life. He did this not because of anything we had done, but because of his own plan and grace. He gave us this grace in Christ Jesus before time began.
But now he has made it known through the coming of our Saviour, Christ Jesus. Christ has destroyed death, and through the Good News he has brought life that never dies into the light.
For this Good News I was chosen to be a preacher, an apostle and a teacher of the Gentiles.
That is why I am suffering these things. But I am not ashamed, because I know the one I have believed. I am sure he is able to guard what I have trusted to him until that day.
Keep the pattern of healthy teaching that you heard from me, with the faith and love that are in Christ Jesus.
Guard the good thing that was trusted to you, with the help of the Holy Spirit who lives in us.
You know that everyone in the province of Asia has turned away from me, including Phygelus and Hermogenes.
May the Lord show mercy to the family of Onesiphorus. He often cheered me up, and he was not ashamed that I was in chains.
Instead, when he was in Rome, he searched hard for me until he found me.
May the Lord let him find mercy from the Lord on that day! And you know very well how many ways he helped me in Ephesus.
